Verdict: clean. No blockers. The PR changes `.github/`, so the maintainer decides the merge (`needs-maintainer` class). This review sets no label.

## Checks

1. **Triggers.** `post-merge.yml` keeps only `push` on `branches: [main]` and `workflow_dispatch`. The PR adds no `push`, `pull_request`, `pull_request_target` or `schedule` trigger. A fork PR cannot start a job on a self-hosted runner.
2. **Secrets, permissions, actions.** No new secret or variable. Permissions do not change: top level `contents: read`, the gate job `contents/actions/pull-requests: read`, only the report job has `issues: write`. The actions are the same as on main (`actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/upload-artifact@v4`, `actions/download-artifact@v4`).
3. **Concurrency and runners.**
   - The workflow group is `post-merge-${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}` with `cancel-in-progress: false`. The report job has the job group `post-merge-report`, also with `cancel-in-progress: false`.
   - The two jobs use `runs-on: [self-hosted, camcraft-post-merge]`. Today 8 online runners have that label (`cheese`, `dude`, `skull`, `egg`, `len-pm`, `uma`, `wopr`, `wopr-2`). None of them has `camcraft-pr-test`. Only `m3` has `camcraft-pr-test`. Thus a post-merge run never takes a PR test runner.
   - The Linux post-merge runners also match `cut.yml` (`[self-hosted, linux]`). This is not new. The yield step (`post-merge-skip.sh`) still applies at the start of each gate.
   - Queue: a burst of merges queues one run for each commit, with no upper limit. GitHub fails a self-hosted job that waits more than 24 h. At about 20 min for each gate and 8 runners, this is acceptable for the merge rate of this repository.
   - The report group keeps one pending job. A third waiting report cancels the middle one. The decision file records this limit. The next report on main corrects the state, thus this is acceptable.
4. **Order marker in `post-merge-report.sh`.**
   - The marker regex accepts only 7-40 hex digits (line 64). Text that a person writes in the issue body cannot get into a git command.
   - The skip occurs only when the two shas resolve, are different, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` is true (lines 66-69). If `rev-parse` or `merge-base` fails, the run reports as before (fail open to a report).
   - The report checkout has `fetch-depth: 0` (workflow line 133). `actions/checkout` then fetches all branch heads, thus a newer marker commit on main is in the clone.
   - Out-of-order results are correct: an older green run does not close a newer red issue, an older red run does not open an issue after a newer green run, and a re-run of the same commit reports.
5. **Shell safety.** No `run:` block has a `${{ }}` expression. All values go through `env:`. The script uses no commit message, branch name or issue text in a command. All variables are quoted. The script has `set -uo pipefail` without `-e`, as on main. Each write has `|| exit 1`.
6. **Tests** (own worktree at `0e2380d33`, Windows, `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1`, `-j 18`):
   - `post_merge_concurrency::post_merge_runs_each_commit_on_its_own`: pass.
   - `post_merge_concurrency::post_merge_reports_one_at_a_time_with_full_history`: pass.
   - `post_merge_report::a_failed_gate_still_runs_the_report_job`: pass.
   - `post_merge_report::order::*` (6 tests): not run by cargo. They are `#[cfg(unix)]` and do not compile on Windows. I ran the same 6 scenarios by hand in Git Bash against the real script and the same fake `gh`. All 6 gave the expected writes. A seventh case (a marker sha that git does not know) closed the issue as before (fail open).
7. **Process law.** The PR changes `xtask/tests/`. The body has `Process change: yes`. The PR does not change `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`. The decision file `docs/decisions/3184-post-merge-per-commit.md` is present.

## Notes (not blockers)

- `set_marker` (lines 54-60): `issue_body` returns an empty string when `gh issue view` fails (`|| true`). Then `issue edit --body` replaces the full issue body with the marker only. The failing steps of the first red run are then lost from the body. Recommendation: stop `set_marker` when the read fails, or skip the edit when the body is empty.
- Line 41: the `--state all` list takes the first result as the newest issue. The script does not give a sort order. When an issue is open, use `$open` as the marker issue first. Alternatively add `sort:created-desc` to the search.
- `.claude/skills/runners/SKILL.md` still says "A group of merges tests only the newest head (`cancel-in-progress`)". The PR body names this follow-up, but no issue for it is open. File a `P7` follow-up issue.

Coordinator: the maintainer decided this PR in his own words: "review and push thru PR 3185". The review that this merge relies on is comment 7069026569 (clean, read-only Opus, head 0e2380d33). The PR has no refresh after that review (class SAME, no new commits). I flag it ready and merge it on head 0e2380d33. Nothing is pushed after this flag.
